title: Greg Errico on Sly and the Family Stone's Fantastic, Forgotten Concert Document Live at the Fillmore East (Robin Tolleson, Modern Drummer, 17 September 2015)
notes: "I started playing when I was fourteen, and I'm self-taught." Played along to records in his basement while friends worked from method books: "I'd put on everything from Xavier Cugat to Buddy Rich." The youngest in the band, at seventeen and a half. With Larry Graham, "natural chemistry": they learned when the bass drum and bass should lock and when to play counterparts. On the Fillmore sets, "strong double-time beats and outstanding kick work".

title: Sly & The Family Stone - Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin), a US television performance, 1969-70 (YouTube ImDxjn8tcYY, an upscaled upload)
notes: Looked at frame by frame (0:00-5:00): Errico at a kit whose white front head reads "SLY AND THE FAMILY STONE" in stacked wavy letters; the toms in black, studded all over with rows of small white dots; chrome hardware. Long, curly brown hair, round tinted glasses, a lime-green blouse with full sleeves under a gold patterned waistcoat. The show is not named in the upload.

title: Stand! (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Personnel: Greg Errico, drums. After an acetate drew a lukewarm reaction in a San Francisco club, Sly recut the song's final section, a gospel break: "Most of the Family Stone was unavailable for the session, and Stone resorted to using mostly studio musicians for the rerecorded section."

title: Sing a Simple Song - Wikipedia
notes: The B-side of Everyday People (1968), on Stand! (1969). Personnel: Greg Errico, drums.

title: I Want to Take You Higher - Wikipedia
notes: On Stand! (1969), the B-side of Stand!, reissued as a single in 1970 after Woodstock. Personnel: Greg Errico, drums, background vocals.

title: Life (Sly and the Family Stone album) - Wikipedia
notes: 1968. "Much of Life has been heavily sampled for hip hop and electronica recordings, particularly Gregg Errico's drum solo on 'Love City'." Personnel: Greg Errico, drums.
